## Research Interests

My research sits at the intersection of **health economics, demographic behavior, and the political economy of labor and public policy** — with a focus on environmental health, global health financing, and inequality in low-resource settings. Methodologically, I specialize in quasi-experimental designs (RDD, DiD), DHS-based survey analysis, and computational text analysis, with all empirical work implemented in R.

## Working Papers

**Sarker, P., & Lin, Y.** (2026). *Loss and Longing: Fertility Preferences Following Child Loss.*
Presented: Population Association of America 2026.

> This paper examines how experiencing child loss shapes subsequent fertility preferences using nationally representative DHS data from Bangladesh. I analyze how demographic, socioeconomic, and household factors interact with reproductive preferences after loss, contributing to demographic research and reproductive health policy.

---

**Sarker, P., & Bin Kamal, K.** (2026). *Wrongful Discharge Laws and Firm Productivity: Evidence from Quasi-Experimental Variation in Employment Protection.*
Selected: Midwest Political Science Association 2026.

> This paper studies how the adoption of wrongful discharge laws affects labor productivity and firm outcomes. Leveraging state-level policy variation, I use quasi-experimental methods to assess dynamic effects over time, contributing to the political economy of labor regulation and institutional design.

---

**Sarker, P.** (2026). *Donor Dependence, PEPFAR, and Drug Pricing: Political Economy of Global Health Financing in Low-Resource Settings.*

---

**Sarker, P.** (2026). *Media Framing of Immigration Enforcement: Ideological Variation Across Major U.S. News Outlets.*

> This project uses computational text analysis to examine how major U.S. news outlets frame immigration enforcement differently across the ideological spectrum. Using corpus construction, document-feature matrices, and quanteda scaling models, I identify systematic variation in framing that maps onto outlet ideology.

## Methods & Technical Skills

**Causal Inference & Econometrics**
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD and Fuzzy RDD), Difference-in-Differences, panel data methods, quasi-experimental designs, robustness testing

**Survey & Demographic Analysis**
DHS multi-wave data, sampling weights, weighted regression and logistic models, field instrument design

**Computational Text Analysis**
Corpus construction, document-feature matrices, quanteda scaling models, tidytext

**Software**
R (advanced) · Stata (intermediate) · SPSS · ODK/SurveyCTO · Git/GitHub
